I did not make any changes — this is the reconnaissance report.

## What the object is called

There is one domain object with **two names split by language**, and crimes named the split for me:

```
Cross-Language Concept Alias Drift  ·  packages/api/billing/plans.py:10
  · concept group "tenant" is named differently on each side of the boundary
  · Python uses: team
  · TypeScript uses: workspace
  · preferred form for this group: "organization"
```

So: **`team` (Python) ≡ `workspace` (TypeScript) ≡ the tenant**. crimes' suggested canonical form is `organization`, which is a *third* name — picking it means renaming both sides rather than surrendering one to the other.

## Every site you'd have to touch

crimes enumerated 8 of them; the truncated `…+1 more` is `changeWorkspacePlan()` at `workspace-client.ts:33`. Reading the files confirms the full set:

**Python — `team` (5 sites + 4 route paths)**
- `packages/api/billing/plans.py:11` — docstring "The tiers a **team** can be on"
- `packages/api/billing/routes.py:11,16,21,26` — `get_team`, `create_team`, `team_seats`, `change_team_plan`, plus every `team_id` parameter
- Route paths: `/api/teams`, `/api/teams/{team_id}`, `/api/teams/{team_id}/seats`, `/api/teams/{team_id}/plan`

**TypeScript — `workspace` (6 sites)**
- `packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:12` — `interface Workspace`
- `:17, :22, :27, :33` — `getWorkspace`, `createWorkspace`, `workspaceSeats`, `changeWorkspacePlan`
- The filename itself, `workspace-client.ts`

## What else you'd have to touch — the parts that make this not a rename

**1. The wire format is a third naming axis, and it's already broken.** The URLs are not consistent with either side's identifiers. crimes caught one:

```
Cross-Language Route Drift  ·  workspace-client.ts:23
  · 1 frontend call reaches a path no backend route declares
  · packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:23 — POST /api/workspaces
  · 4 backend routes declared across 1 file
  · matched on literal path strings — a route or URL assembled at runtime is
    invisible to this check
```

That last evidence line is a disclaimer worth acting on. Following it to line 18 finds a **second** broken call crimes could not see — `fetch("/api/workspaces/" + id)` is string-concatenated, so it's invisible to the literal matcher, and it's just as 404 as line 23. The frontend is mid-rename: two calls already say `/api/workspaces`, two still say `/api/teams`. **Renaming the routes is a breaking public API change, not an internal rename** — that's the piece that decides whether this is a one-PR job or needs versioning/redirects.

**2. There is a collision trap: `team` is also a plan tier.**

```
Cross-Language Type Drift  ·  Plan  (high)
  · packages/api/billing/plans.py:10 — Plan declares [free, pro, team, scale]
  · packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:10 — Plan declares [free, pro, enterprise]
  · only in Python: scale, team — the TypeScript side will reject these values
  · only in TypeScript: enterprise — the Python side will reject this value
```

`plans.py:15` is `TEAM = "team"` — a **plan name**, not the tenant. A global `team → organization` rename corrupts `Plan.TEAM`, the string literal `"team"`, and the `SEATS_INCLUDED` key at `plans.py:22`. Any sed-style rename must exclude the `Plan` enum. This is the highest-severity finding in the repo and it's entangled with the rename rather than adjacent to it.

**3. Two more contract mismatches sit in the same blast area** and would be easy to "accidentally fix" or accidentally cement mid-rename:
- `Cross-Language Route Drift` — frontend sends `PUT /api/teams/:id/plan`, backend declares `POST`. crimes notes this "fails as a 405 rather than a 404 — easy to misread as a permissions problem."
- `False Identity` — `getWorkspace` reads as pure but calls `fetch`. Whatever you rename it to, the `get` prefix carries the same lie forward.

**4. Nothing will catch you if you get it wrong.** Every one of the 5 findings scores `test_gap: 1.0` and `blast_radius: 0`. crimes' coverage block reports 3 source files total, 0 test files. There is no test to run after the rename.

## Two workflow notes

- `crimes context packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts` re-rooted at `packages/web` and reported **MEDIUM, 1 finding** — it dropped all three cross-language findings. For a polyglot rename, scan from the monorepo root; per-file `context` under-reports here.
- crimes' own suggested action is the right instinct: *"generate one side from the other, or share a schema… Keeping two hand-maintained copies in sync is the thing that already failed here."* The `Plan` drift is proof the manual-sync approach already failed once.

## My read on scope

This is not a rename, it's a contract unification, and I'd sequence it: **(a)** decide the canonical name and whether the HTTP paths change (that's a product/compat call, not a mechanical one); **(b)** fix the `Plan` enum drift *first*, in isolation, since it's the high finding and it booby-traps the rename; **(c)** add at least a contract test before touching identifiers, because right now nothing verifies either side; **(d)** then rename, treating `Plan.TEAM` as an explicit exclusion.

Tell me which name you want to standardise on — `organization` (crimes' suggestion), `team`, or `workspace` — and whether the API paths are allowed to break, and I'll do the change.
